It is the immediate caller in the override path, and therefore a strong surface/intermediate candidate for wrong ordering or context of the exception-spec check during class/template completion. It is less specific than rank #1 because the exact error text is emitted in the callee, but it remains very close to the failure.

This is the high-level class semantic entry point that triggers look_for_overrides for a declaration in a class. The bug appears during class template override checking before passes, and this function initiates that path. It is likely upstream rather than the root cause, but if GCC is checking an override too early for a dependent noexcept case, this call path is directly involved.

This helper queries whether a function type is noexcept from TYPE_RAISES_EXCEPTIONS and asserts that the spec is not deferred. If deferred/dependent forms are being mishandled upstream, this predicate can misclassify the final type-level state used in comparisons. It is smaller and less comprehensive than build_noexcept_spec or tsubst_exception_specification, but very close to the actual boolean classification at issue.

This function iterates class methods and calls check_for_override on each, making it a plausible upstream trigger during class completion. The issue is a compile-time diagnostic on virtual member overrides in class templates, and this function sits exactly at that semantic phase. It does not implement noexcept logic itself, so it ranks below the specific search/pt/except methods.

ranked_methods.signature: static tree tsubst_function_type (tree t, tree args, tsubst_flags_t complain, tree in_decl)
ranked_methods.reason: This method rebuilds substituted function or method types and delegates to rebuild_function_or_method_type with raises=NULL_TREE. For a bug about exception specifications on overridden member function types, function-type rebuilding is relevant, especially if exception-spec state is intentionally delayed and later reconstructed. It is less directly tied to the exact diagnostic than tsubst_exception_specification or maybe_instantiate_noexcept, but still a strong upstream mechanism candidate.
